cor.heading: Cost of sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales decreased to 26.9% of total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven by lower amortization expense from acquisition-related assets and lower manufacturing costs, partially offset by higher profit share expense and changes in our sales mix.

Cost of sales decreased to 28.7% of total revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, driven by lower amortization expense from acquisition-related assets, partially offset by higher profit share expense and changes in our sales mix.

opex.text: Operating expenses were as follows (dollar amounts in millions):

costs.heading: Operating expenses
costs.text: Operating expenses were as follows (dollar amounts in millions):

rd.heading: Research and development
rd.text:
The increase in R&D expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was driven by higher spend in Research and Early Pipeline, including business development activity.

The increase in R&D expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was driven by higher spend in Research and Early Pipeline, including business development activity, and Later-Stage Clinical Programs, primarily those related to MariTide.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative
ga.text: The decreases in SG&A expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, were driven by lower general and administrative expenses, partially offset by higher commercial product-related expenses.

sga.heading: Selling, general and administrative
sga.text: The decreases in SG&A expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, were driven by lower general and administrative expenses, partially offset by higher commercial product-related expenses.

other_opex.text: Other operating expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, included intangible asset impairment charges, and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, also included certain items associated with legal proceedings.

nonint.heading: Operating expenses
nonint.text: Operating expenses were as follows (dollar amounts in millions):

nonop.heading: Interest expense, net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net, remained relatively unchanged for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Interest expense, net, decreased for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to lower average debt outstanding.

tax.heading: Income taxes
tax.text:
The decrease in our effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily due to the change in earnings mix, including lower net unrealized gains on equity investments, partially offset by prior-year period net favorable items as compared to the current-year period. The increase in our effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily due to the prior year Otezla intangible asset impairment charges and net unfavorable items in the current-year period as compared to the prior-year period, partially offset by the change in earnings mix, including lower net unrealized gains on equity investments and lower amortization expense from acquisition-related assets.

In 2021, the OECD reached an initial agreement to align countries on a minimum corporate tax rate and an expansion of the taxing rights of market countries. Select individual countries, including the United Kingdom, EU member countries and Singapore, have enacted the global minimum tax agreement that took effect starting in 2024. Singapore’s enactment of the agreement effective 2025 applies irrespective of the Company’s incentive grant. On January 5, 2026, the OECD issued administrative guidance related to the global minimum tax agreement that, when fully enacted, will exempt U.S. companies from extra territorial minimum taxes effective January 1, 2026.

ocf.text: Cash provided by operating activities has been and is expected to continue to be our primary recurring source of funds. Cash provided by operating activities during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased as compared to the same period in the prior year primarily due to the final $1.8 billion repatriation tax payment in the second quarter of 2025 and higher net income in the current-year period after adjustments for noncash items, partially offset by the timing of working capital items.

da.text: Certain of our financing arrangements contain nonfinancial covenants. In addition, our revolving credit agreement and term loan credit agreement include a financial covenant that requires us to maintain a specified minimum interest coverage ratio of (i) the sum of consolidated net income, interest expense, provision for income taxes, depreciation expense, amortization expense, unusual or nonrecurring charges and other noncash items (consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) to (ii) Consolidated Interest Expense, each as defined and described in the respective agreements. We were in compliance with all applicable covenants under these arrangements as of September 30, 2026.

wc.text: We believe that existing funds, cash generated from operations and existing sources of and access to financing are adequate to satisfy our needs for working capital, capital expenditure and debt service requirements, as well as our plans to pay dividends and repurchase stock, and other business initiatives we plan to strategically pursue, including acquisitions and licensing activities. We anticipate that our liquidity needs can be met through a variety of sources, including cash provided by operating activities, borrowings through commercial paper and/or syndicated credit facilities and access to other domestic and foreign debt markets and equity markets. See Part II, Item 1A. Risk Factors— Global economic conditions may negatively affect us and may magnify certain risks that affect our business, of our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.

capex.text: Consistent with the objective to optimize our capital structure, we deploy our accumulated cash balances in a strategic manner and consider a number of alternatives, including investments in innovation both internally and externally (including investments that expand our portfolio of products in areas of therapeutic interest), capital expenditures, repayment of debt, payment of dividends and stock repurchases.

intro.text: Amgen discovers, develops, manufactures and delivers innovative medicines to fight some of the world’s toughest diseases. Harnessing the best of biology and technology, Amgen reaches millions of patients with its medicines. More than 45 years ago, Amgen helped establish the biotechnology industry at its U.S. headquarters in Thousand Oaks, California, and it remains at the cutting edge of innovation, using technology and human genetic data to push beyond what is known today. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases and obesity and obesity-related conditions.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

We depend on alliances with other companies, including pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, vendors and service providers, for the development of a portion of the products in our pharmaceutical pipeline and for the commercialization and sales of certain of our commercial products.
We rely on unaffiliated third-party suppliers for certain raw materials, medical devices and components necessary for the manufacturing of our commercial and clinical products.

Certain of those raw materials, medical devices and components are proprietary products of those unaffiliated third-party suppliers and are specifically cited in our drug applications with regulatory agencies so that they must be obtained from that specific sole source or sources and could not be obtained from another supplier unless and until the regulatory agency approved such supplier.
For example, we rely on a single source for the SureClick autoinjectors used in the drug delivery of a number of our products, including Repatha and ENBREL.

These efforts often rely on a single or limited number of vendors and suppliers, and identifying or qualifying alternatives may not be feasible or may require significant time and expense due to the specialized nature of our manufacturing requirements.

Further, we rely on commercial transportation, including air and sea freight, for the distribution of our products to our customers, which has been negatively affected by pandemics, labor unrest, natural disasters and geopolitical security threats.

Further, many of our key facilities are located on islands, including Puerto Rico, Singapore and Ireland, which rely on essential port facilities that may be vulnerable to climate change-related or other natural disasters.

s.t: As of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, our ownership interest in BeOne was approximately 17 % and the fair values of our investment were $ 6.9 billion and $ 5.8 billion, respectively, which were included in Other noncurrent assets in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets.

Excluding our equity investment in BeOne (discussed above), we held investments in other equity securities with readily determinable fair values (publicly traded securities) of $ 398 million and $ 389 million as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively, which were included in Other noncurrent assets in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets.

The fair values of our money market mutual funds and equity investments in publicly traded securities, including our equity investment in BeOne, as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, are based on quoted market prices in active markets, with no valuation adjustment.

s.t: The increase in Other income, net, for 2025 was primarily due to current year net unrealized gains on equity investments, primarily BeOne, compared to net unrealized losses on equity investments in the prior year.

The 2023 net unrealized gains on equity investments were principally composed of amounts recognized on our BeOne investment in the first quarter of 2023 as a result of a change from the equity method of accounting to recording this investment at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in earnings.
For information on a collaboration agreement we entered into with BeOne in connection with this investment, see Note 9, Collaborations.

Subject to certain exceptions or otherwise agreed to by BeOne, while Amgen holds at least 5.0 % of BeOne’s outstanding common stock, (A) we may only sell our BeOne equity investment via: (i) a registered public offering, (ii) a sale under Rule 144 of the Securities Act of 1933 (the “Securities Act”) or (iii) a private sale exempt from registration requirements under the Securities Act, and (B) we may not sell more than 5.0 % of BeOne’s outstanding common stock in any rolling 12-month period.

As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, our ownership interest in Neumora was approximately 21.2 % and 21.9 %, respectively, and the fair values of our investment were $ 63 million and $ 375 million, respectively, which were included in Other noncurrent assets in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.

The fair values of our money market mutual funds and equity investments in publicly traded securities, including our equity investments in BeOne and Neumora, as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, are based on quoted market prices in active markets, with no valuation adjustment .
